course_description:
Working on complex software systems and ensuring those systems remain maintainable requires disciplined, individual software development practices. Software must be well-specified, well-implemented and well-tested. This course covers concepts and techniques in modern programming languages that help support good software development practice (such as OO concepts, genericity and exception handling) with specific application to file IO and GUIs in Java.

This course utilises the Java programming language to introduce students to object-oriented programming, including concepts such as data abstraction, specification, and unit testing. This is not a Java programming course. The focus of the course is object-oriented programming, while using Java to achieve this. The lecture topics include Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) (classes and objects), inheritance and polymorphism, packages, collections, exception handling, unit testing, programming by contract, I/O, parsing files and folders, GUIs (event handlers, buttons, tables, lists, etc.), design quality, coupling, cohesion, GUI design principles, model-view-controller variants, generics, lambda expressions, streams, recursion and iteration, sorting, and textual analysis.

AI tools are used as part of normal work or professional practices in this course. AI use is part of assessed work. Students are expected to consider AI in an appropriate way, to interpret and check any AI-generated outputs, and to take responsibility for the quality and correctness of their work. Students are responsible for ensuring that any use of AI complies with academic integrity requirements and is appropriately acknowledged.

Software must be well-specified, well-implemented and well-tested. This course covers concepts and techniques in modern programming languages that help support good practice (such as OO concepts, genericity and exception handling) in Java.

learning_outcomes.description: Implement object-oriented programs according to their specifications.
Design, implement and document object-oriented programs using language features such as inheritance, interfaces, polymorphism, exceptions and I/O.
Design and implement test components for object-oriented programs.
Analyse code to judge whether it follows good programming practice.
Write, interpret and critique specifications for program modules (e.g. classes or interfaces).

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
These problem sets will be delivered and submitted via the Ed Lessons online environment. A link to this environment is available on Blackboard.
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
To accommodate unforeseen circumstances, including delayed enrolment, delayed attendance, illness, or other life events, your mark will be based on your best 10 out of the 12 possible submissions. Any missing submissions are calculated as zero marks for that submission.
Because only the best 10 of 12 will contribute to the mark for this assessment item and the answers are released on the due date, no extensions are permitted .
Late submission
You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late .
To accommodate unforeseen circumstances, your mark will be based on your best 10 out of the 12 possible submissions.
Because the answers are released immediately at the due date and time and only the best 10 of 12 possible submissions will contribute to the mark for this assessment item an immediate 100% penalty will be applied to late submission . To avoid confusion with other assessment rules in other courses, there can be no grace period as the answers are already released. Any late submissions are awarded zero marks for that submission.
This has been approved by the Associate Dean (Academic)

A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. A portion of the Assignment 1 marking and feedback is immediate on every submission and every re-submission, giving students instantaneous feedback on more than a quarter of the overall Assignment 1 assessment. Note that the due date for Assignment 1 is before the Census date. This gives students submitting by the due date the opportunity to receive immediate feedback before the Census date.
